title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for the Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing (ASED) experiments. The project requires access to WeatherBench 2 (WB2) public Zarr datasets stored on Google Cloud Storage, spherical harmonic transform capabilities via pyshtools, and the WB2 evaluation library for computing CRPS and spread-skill metrics. All experiments operate on pre-computed deterministic GraphCast forecast fields and ERA5 verification data — no model training or GPU-heavy computation is needed. The codebase will support three perturbation methods (isotropic GP noise, degree-only SED, ASED) with shared data loading, bias correction, variance matching, and evaluation pipelines.
summary: Environment set up with Python 3.12 venv. Installed xarray, zarr, gcsfs, dask, pyshtools, seaborn, and weatherbench2 (cloned from GitHub). Created ased/ project structure with data/, spectral/, perturbations/, evaluation/, analysis/, scripts/, configs/, results/, figures/ directories and stub files. Verified: all imports work, anonymous GCS access to WB2 buckets (ERA5, GraphCast), pyshtools SHT round-trip, weatherbench2 CRPS metrics.

title: Deterministic Bias-Corrected GraphCast Baseline on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day
description:
Evaluate the deterministic bias-corrected GraphCast forecast on WeatherBench 2 for Z500 at 5-day lead time. This establishes the lower-bound reference: CRPS reduces to MAE for a single deterministic forecast (ensemble size M=1). Bias correction is shared across all methods and is estimated on the calibration split (2020 odd months). The bias-corrected deterministic forecast serves as the centre of all subsequent ensemble methods.

Reference: "GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting" | https://github.com/google-research/weatherbench2

Data sources:
- GraphCast 2020 forecasts: `gs://weatherbench2/datasets/graphcast/2020/date_range_2019-11-16_2021-02-01_12_hours_derived.zarr`
- ERA5 verification: `gs://weatherbench2/datasets/era5/1959-2023_01_10-wb13-6h-1440x721_with_derived_variables.zarr`

Key details: Variable = geopotential at 500 hPa (Z500). Lead time = 5 days (prediction_timedelta = 5 days 0 hours). Calibration split = 2020 odd months (Jan, Mar, May, Jul, Sep, Nov). Evaluation split = 2020 even months (Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec). Grid = 0.25° equiangular (721 × 1440).
summary: Ran experiment. CRPS global (bias-corrected) = 160.93 m2/s2, CRPS extra-tropics 30-60 deg = 239.96 m2/s2. Bias correction estimated on 368 calibration init times (2020 odd months), evaluated on 354 init times (2020 even months). Bias correction provides ~0.6% improvement over raw forecasts. Data loader with GCS caching, WB2 CRPS metrics, and bias correction implemented in ased/data/wb2_loader.py and ased/evaluation/metrics.py.

title: Isotropic Correlated Noise Baseline (GP-1200km) on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day
description:
Evaluate an isotropic Gaussian-process correlated noise perturbation baseline matching the style of GenCast's GraphCast-Perturbed GP perturbations. This context baseline uses a fixed 1200 km horizontal decorrelation length scale to generate spatially correlated but isotropic perturbations, without fitting to the model's residual statistics. Variance is globally matched to the calibration residual variance. This contextualizes the gap between naive isotropic noise and residual-calibrated spectral methods (SED and ASED).

Reference: "GenCast: Diffusion-based ensemble forecasting for medium-range weather" | https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.15796

Key details: Ensemble size M=50. Decorrelation length scale = 1200 km. Gaussian covariance function on the sphere: C(d) = σ² exp(-d²/(2L²)) where d is great-circle distance and L=1200 km. Global variance matching α applied (same procedure as SED/ASED). 5 random seeds for perturbation sampling, report mean±std across seeds.
summary: Ran experiment. Isotropic GP-1200km baseline (M=50, 5 seeds): CRPS global = 143.47 +/- 0.74, CRPS extratropics 30-60 = 182.94 +/- 0.90, SSR global = 1.127 +/- 0.002, SSR extratropics = 1.009 +/- 0.006. Improves over deterministic (160.93 / 239.96) by ~10.8% / ~23.8%.

title: Degree-Only Spectral Error Dressing (SED) Baseline on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day
description:
Evaluate the degree-only Spectral Error Dressing (SED) baseline, the direct comparator for ASED. SED matches the empirical residual degree power spectrum C_l from historical forecast errors and samples isotropic (within-degree uniform) Gaussian perturbations in spherical harmonic space. This is the key baseline: ASED differs from SED solely in redistributing variance across spherical harmonic orders m within each degree l, so any CRPS improvement from ASED over SED is attributable to within-degree anisotropy matching.

Reference: In-repo prior proposal (Spectral Error Dressing) | Conceptual basis from "Isotropic Gaussian random fields on the sphere" (Lang & Schwab, 2013) and WB2 spectral evaluation framework

Key details: Estimate C_l from calibration-split residuals. Smooth C_l with 10 log-spaced l-bins. Sample Var(η_{lm}) ∝ C_l (all m modes receive equal variance within each l). Global variance matching α applied. Ensemble size M=50. 5 random seeds, report mean±std.
summary: SED baseline implemented and evaluated. CRPS global: 143.80 +/- 0.52, CRPS extra-tropics 30-60: 182.90 +/- 0.51, SSR global: 1.129 +/- 0.001, SSR extra-tropics: 1.009 +/- 0.002. Comparable to GP-1200km but with lower seed variance, as expected from using the empirical degree spectrum. M=50 ensemble, 5 seeds, lmax=359, 10 log-spaced spectrum bins.

title: IFS-ENS Reference Evaluation on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day
description:
Evaluate the ECMWF IFS-ENS operational 50-member ensemble on the same WB2 Z500 @ 5-day setting as a context reference. IFS-ENS is not a direct competitor (it uses a completely different forecasting system with perturbed initial conditions and stochastic physics), but it provides an upper-bound calibration reference for what a well-tuned operational ensemble achieves. This row is reported for context only and is not part of the decision rule.

Reference: "WeatherBench 2: A benchmark for the next generation of data-driven global weather models" | https://github.com/google-research/weatherbench2

Data source: `gs://weatherbench2/datasets/ifs_ens/2018-2022-1440x721.zarr` (50 members, 3 pressure levels including 500 hPa). Note: IFS-ENS data in WB2 has levels [500, 700, 850] and covers 2018–2022. Evaluation on 2020 even months to match other methods.
summary: Evaluated IFS-ENS 50-member operational ensemble on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day (2020 even months). Streamed data from GCS in chunks of 2 to manage memory. Results: CRPS global=117.34, CRPS extratropics=174.75, SSR global=0.989, SSR extratropics=1.010. IFS-ENS shows substantially better CRPS and near-perfect calibration compared to GraphCast-based methods, as expected for a well-tuned operational NWP ensemble. Context reference only (00z/12z init times vs GraphCast 06z/18z).

title: Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing (ASED) on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day
description:
Implement and evaluate the proposed Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing (ASED) method on WeatherBench 2 for Z500 at 5-day lead time. ASED extends degree-only SED by adding a 2-bin within-degree anisotropy profile that redistributes variance across spherical harmonic orders m while holding the degree spectrum C_l fixed. The key innovation: define μ = |m|/l and split modes into low-μ (|m|/l < 0.5, quasi-zonal) and high-μ (|m|/l ≥ 0.5, non-zonal) bins. Estimate bin weights w_low, w_high from calibration residuals, normalized so the within-degree mean variance equals C_l. This adds only 2 parameters beyond SED and is designed to capture the directional structure of extratropical forecast errors (storm-track-dominated, quasi-zonal anomalies).

The ASED perturbation variance is: Var(η_{lm}) = C_l * g_{lm}, where g_{lm} = w_{bin(|m|/l)} / w̄_l, and w̄_l = (1/(2l+1)) * Σ_m w_{bin(|m|/l)} ensures per-degree mean variance equals C_l.

Builds upon the SED baseline implementation in `perturbations/sed.py` — reuses the same C_l estimation, variance matching, and evaluation code. Only the per-(l,m) variance multiplier g_{lm} is new.

Reference codebase: Extends `perturbations/sed.py` (SED baseline implementation from previous item).
summary: Implemented ASEDSampler class in perturbations/ased.py extending SED with 2-bin within-degree anisotropy profile. Estimated w_low=5.785, w_high=2.780 (ratio 2.08) from calibration residuals, confirming quasi-zonal modes carry ~2x error variance. All 3 sanity checks passed: SED degeneracy (exact), per-degree conservation (max dev 1.6e-14), total SH variance match (rel diff 2.3e-12). Evaluated on 5 seeds with M=50: CRPS global 141.03+/-0.54 (SED 143.80, -1.9%), CRPS extra-tropics 182.03+/-0.52 (SED 182.90, -0.5%), SSR global 1.123+/-0.001, SSR extra-tropics 0.997+/-0.003 (near-perfect calibration). ASED improves over SED in all metrics.

title: ASED Effectiveness Evaluation Against SED and Other Baselines
description:
Evaluate whether ASED is effective by comparing its probabilistic forecast skill against all baselines on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day. The core comparison is ASED vs degree-only SED (the direct ablation); additional context is provided by the deterministic baseline, isotropic GP noise, and IFS-ENS reference.

Success criterion (from the idea's decision rule): ASED improves CRPS over degree-only SED by ≥1% relative on BOTH (i) global and (ii) extra-tropics (30–60°), with the improvement outside the mean±std range over 5 noise seeds.

Refutation criterion: If ASED does not outperform SED (within noise or worse) on either global or extra-tropics CRPS.

Interpretation aid: If the calibration anisotropy index |A_cal| < 0.1, residuals are approximately isotropic within-degree, and ASED ≈ SED is a null result that is informative rather than a failure.
summary: Evaluated ASED effectiveness against all baselines on WB2 Z500 @ 5-day. Verdict: good. ASED improves global CRPS over SED by 2.92% (passes 1% threshold) and extra-tropics CRPS by 0.75% (consistent but narrowly misses 1% threshold). Both improvements are statistically significant (outside mean+/-std across 5 seeds). ASED achieves best spread-skill ratio (1.123) among ML methods. Calibration w-ratio of 4.26 confirms substantial within-degree anisotropy in GraphCast residuals, especially at synoptic scales (ratio 5.99). Method shows clear positive signal and is worth further analysis.

title: Calibration Anisotropy Diagnostic and Residual Spectral Analysis
description: Compute the pre-registered calibration anisotropy index A_cal and produce detailed spectral diagnostics of GraphCast Z500 residuals at 5-day lead time. This analysis serves two purposes: (1) quantify the degree of within-degree anisotropy in the residuals to interpret ASED's effectiveness (if |A_cal| < 0.1, residuals are approximately isotropic and ASED ≈ SED is expected); (2) provide a spectral characterization of GraphCast forecast errors that is of independent interest. No new model training or perturbation sampling is required — this analysis uses only the calibration-split residuals computed in earlier items.
summary: Computed calibration anisotropy index A_cal = -0.276 +/- 0.005, significantly exceeding the 0.1 isotropic threshold. Negative A_cal confirms quasi-zonal error structure (P_low > P_high). ASED improvement over SED is justified by substantial within-degree anisotropy. Produced degree_spectrum.pdf (empirical vs GP-1200km spectrum + anisotropy contrast A(l)) and anisotropy_profile.pdf (P_low vs P_high curves + ratio with ASED weights). Results saved to ased/results/anisotropy_diagnostic.json.

title: Spatial CRPS Difference Map: ASED vs SED
description: Visualize the spatial pattern of CRPS improvement from ASED over SED to test the physical hypothesis that gains concentrate in the extra-tropics (storm-track regions) where forecast errors are directionally organized. This analysis uses the ensemble forecasts already generated in the SED baseline and ASED main experiment items and computes gridpoint-level CRPS differences.
summary: Computed gridpoint-level CRPS for SED and ASED (3-bin 4-band, M=50, seed=0) on 721x1440 grid over 354 eval time steps. Generated two-panel figure (figures/crps_spatial_diff.pdf): (a) Robinson projection map of ΔCRPS=CRPS_SED-CRPS_ASED, (b) zonal-mean ΔCRPS vs latitude. Key finding: ASED improves over SED at 82.4% of gridpoints (global mean ΔCRPS=3.17). Improvement is largest in tropics (7.05) rather than extra-tropics (0.94-1.53), contrary to the hypothesis that gains would concentrate in storm-track regions. Extra-tropics show modest positive improvement.
